 National | 9 hours ago Dengue: Record 2,249 patients hospitalised, 7 die in 24hrs
 FE ONLINE DESK
 Published :
 Oct 25, 2026, 11:31 
 Bangladesh recorded 2,249 dengue cases in the 24 hours to Sunday morning, the highest single-day tally so far this year.
 During the same period, seven people died of the mosquito-borne disease, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), reports UNB.
 The latest figures brought the total number of dengue cases to 123,948 and the death toll to 384 this year.
 Of the new deaths, two each were reported in Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) area and Mymensingh division, while one each was recorded in Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) area, Khulna and Rajshahi divisions.
 Of the total deaths recorded this year, 52.8 per cent were female, and 47.2 per cent were male.
 Earlier, on September 27, Bangladesh recorded its previous highest daily dengue cases of 2,158.
 The highest number of dengue deaths in a single day this year was recorded on October 6 and 15, when 10 people succumbed to the mosquito-borne disease.
 A total of 117,400 dengue patients have been discharged from hospitals after recovery this year, according to the DGHS.
